contexts.text: (Correspondence of the stench of vomit. See Odour.) SE 6100.
Under Bitumen, see this reference.

In the sphere of such stenches are those who are in Hell; and, wonderful to say, those who are in them do not smell the stink; nay, these stinks are delightful to them; and when they are in them they are in the sphere of their delights and deliciousnesses. (Continued. See Odour.)

I perceived his presence from a stink which was like the excrementitious stink of teeth; and a stench was afterwards perceived like that from burning horn or bone... Those who are so natural as not to think anything of spiritual things, not to believe that there is a Hell and a Heaven, and still are subtle in their transactions, are such as these, and are called the unseen natural, being sometimes made manifest to others by their stink. AC 5573. SE 3498.
Under Stomach, see this reference.
(That pirate said) that the fetid stench of urine is what he is most highly delighted with, insomuch that he wants to have his abode in pools, nay, in casks, of fetid urine.
(This Spirit - whose character is here fully described) said that he loves the stench of urine more than all other odours.
The most offensive stench exhaled from the caverns there. (Continued. See Stink.)

Through these caverns are exhaled offensive stenches and stinks, which good Spirits shun... but evil Spirits are eager for... For as in the world everyone has been delighted with his own evil, so after death he is delighted with the stink to which his evil corresponds. In this they may be compared to... ravens, wolves, and swine, which, from the stench which they perceive, fly and run to cadaverous and stercoraceous things. I have heard a certain Spirit crying out aloud as from inward torture when an effluent breathing from Heaven struck him; and tranquil and glad when an effluent breathing from Hell struck him.
They who have been sordidly avaricious... love such stenches as are exhaled from the undigested things of the stomach.
As there are such things in the Hells, they abound in offensive stenches, as cadaverous, stercoraceous, urinous, putrid ones, wherewith the diabolical Spirits there are delighted.

That cadaverous and putrid things are in accord with these noxious and useless animalcules... may be seen from the cause, which is that there are the like stinks and stenches in the Hells, where such animalcules also appear; and therefore these Hells are named from them; some being called cadaverous, some stercoraceous, and so on... Hence it is evident that where there are such stinks, there are such noxious things, because they correspond.
Nidorous, occurs.
See Stink. SE 618. AE 1005:3.
Like the stench in the dens of beasts, which is in congruity with the wild animals there, but not to man unless he is like them.
(The correspondence of a vinous fume. See Wine.)
The persecution of the innocent produces a stench of bed-bugs. Explained.

The delight (of the adulterous and cruel) has now been turned into a stink, that is, into the stench of human ordure, which exhales thence, and which I smell; and they say that there is now such a stench... It is turned into such a stench; and, wonderful to say, the Spirits around me also smell such a stench and stink, as man does in his body. (SE 2625.) At last the stink was so augmented that they said they should perish...
There exhaled from him as it were the stench of garlic. (Its correspondence explained.)

Truths destroyed are falsities, even such falsities as emit a bad smell. From these a stink is perceived in the other life, which is such that it cannot be endured by any good Spirit: it is like the stench of purulent matter from the lungs.

To those who have been assassins and poisoners, and also to those who have perceived delight in rapes, there is nothing more delightful than a cadaverous stench; and to those who have been possessed with the love of exercising command, and also to those who have taken delight in adulteries, and no delight in marriages, there is nothing more delightful than an excrementitious stench; and to those who have confirmed themselves in falsities, and have extinguished in themselves the affection of truth, there is nothing more delightful than a swampy and also a urinous stench.

More than the sweetest odours do (these profaners) love the rank stenches from flatulence and latrines, which to their smell are more fragrant than thyme... In a word, the love of domination by means of the holy things of the Church corresponds to foulness; and its delight to a stink inexpressible in words, and at which the Angels shudder. Such is the exhalation from their Hells when they are opened; but they are kept closed because of the consequent oppression and occasional swooning.
